summary.intent: Land the last review findings on PR #1141 (rotation-cluster crypto fix), get it merged, run /resolve-pr-reviews to clear CodeRabbit/Greptile threads, and keep the wave-7 issue-sequencing plan accurate as #1141's scope and blast radius became clearer.
summary.outcome: PR #1141's six review items were folded in and independently re-verified (fmt/clippy/test/wasm32 all green, 1573 passed/0 failed); PR was marked ready and CodeRabbit review kicked off; /resolve-pr-reviews was launched via a briefed subagent to triage and resolve threads; wave-7 replan was updated for post-merge unblocks, and a #775/mint_grant_row overlap note was corrected from 'worth checking' to 'no current conflict, conditional risk documented' and recorded both as a GitHub comment and in project memory.

repo: ParentScopePlan::identity is now built via a struct update over parent.identity with owner_enc_secret: Some(owner.enc_secret) forced, so callers can no longer pass None and silently disable the parent-leg binding check (crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs:472-479).
ScopeRootIdentity gained #[derive(Clone, Copy)] (crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:65) specifically to support the struct-update pattern above.

mint_grant_row now takes recipient_identity_pk: [u8; IDENTITY_PUBLIC_LEN] instead of a parsed verifier (crates/engine/src/grants/ledger.rs:129-141); parsing it via from_sec1 would let a write-grantee veto the revocation wave, so leaving it uninterpreted is deliberate, not a missing validation.
remint_grants ordering is load-bearing: enforce_committed_ledger must run before minting, or a self-upgraded ledger row could be minted into a commitment the owner then signs.
The non-constant-time tag compare at grants/ledger.rs:74 is intentionally left as-is — the function's own doc states inputs and verdict are public, so ct_eq would contradict the doc and isn't free.

#1141 changed mint_grant_row's signature and made ScopeRootIdentity Copy, so anything touching create.rs, invite.rs, sweep.rs, cascade.rs, or rotate.rs rebases behind it — but #775 specifically only touches gate::floor::AnchorRole, sync/boot.rs, and a new shared-scope cold-seed caller, none of which #1141 touched, so the overlap is conditional (only if #775's cold-seed caller lands in grants/create.rs, grants/invite.rs, or grants/ledger.rs, or constructs a ScopeRootIdentity).

#1136 (scope pointer never renews) was misfiled into the post-merge rotation batch based on its call site (publish_scope_pointer in net/rotation.rs), but its real blocker is HeldRecord's shape — head_cid is a required /ipfs/ head and empty ones are skipped at liveness.rs:245 — same root shape issue as #1144 and #1043.

code.finding: Parent identity leg now forces owner_enc_secret: Some(owner.enc_secret) via struct update to prevent callers from disabling the binding check with None.
mint_grant_row signature changed to take raw recipient_identity_pk bytes instead of a parsed EcdsaVerifier, deliberately avoiding parse-based validation.
Re-mint carries entry.recipient_identity_pk verbatim; from_sec1 parse call removed entirely from rotation.rs.
ScopeRootIdentity derives Clone, Copy to support struct-update identity construction.
Held records with empty head_cid are skipped here — the shape constraint blocking #1136/#1144/#1043.

workflow: When delegating a generic skill (e.g. /resolve-pr-reviews) to a subagent for a repo that doesn't match the skill's assumed stack, explicitly brief the agent on the repo-specific substitutions (Cargo gates instead of pnpm, unpiped output to avoid false passes from tail-truncation) rather than letting it follow the skill verbatim.

For CodeRabbit PR reviews: a posted walkthrough comment is not a completed review — wait for 'Actionable comments posted:' text, and since CodeRabbit edits one status comment in place rather than posting new ones, compare created_at vs updated_at to detect completion.
CodeRabbit nitpicks and verdicts can live in the review body, not just inline threads — both surfaces need reading, not just the threads API.

Before extending a caution/note to another issue (e.g. '#775 should check mint_grant_row changes'), verify file-level overlap by diffing declared scope against actual changed files rather than asserting a plausible-sounding risk.

When a corrected/narrowed finding needs to survive across sessions, record it in two places: as a comment on the relevant GitHub issue (where the future implementer will look) and in project memory (so the next session starts from the plan).

friction: The subagent's initial framing of the #775/mint_grant_row overlap was broader than the evidence supported, requiring a follow-up verification pass (grep against #775's actual declared file scope) before the note could be posted as fact.

#1136 was initially mis-sequenced into the post-merge rotation batch based on surface-level call-site location rather than its actual structural blocker (HeldRecord shape), requiring correction mid-session.
